quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: Before turning, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot.
Look in your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: How much road space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The same full lane width as other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full width of a lane, just like cars and trucks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines are doubled in work zones.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that the road ahead has low clearance for tall vehicles.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving drunk. Stop driving and rest if you feel tired.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that deer may cross the road in this area.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. Any distraction takes your focus away from driving and creates danger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a traffic signal is coming up on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing.
questions.explanation: Yellow diamond-shaped warning signs alert you to hazards. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending or that the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to hazards. This sign tells you a fire station is nearby and to watch for emergency vehicles on the road.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you signal?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. This gives other drivers time to know your plans in advance.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill slope is coming.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down to a stop.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the wheel tightly to stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas. Once you are going slowly, apply the brakes gently and pull safely off the road.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, on curves, when there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. What should drivers know?

options.text: Cars have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has three or more curves coming up.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. This keeps them safe.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns. Do not make a U-turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. Always slow down at railroad crossings. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Road markings:

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.

questions.explanation: Road markings give information to drivers. They help you position your vehicle correctly, show where it is safe to pass, and warn about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave the emergency vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move immediately to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign is:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and usually yellow. Orange warning signs are used in work areas. These signs warn you of dangers ahead or areas where special rules apply.

questions.question: You cannot park:

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
More than 12 inches from the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: There are many places where parking is illegal, including on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the edge.

questions.question: Traffic signs and road markings:

options.text: Only apply when other traffic is present.
Only apply when a police officer is around.

questions.explanation: Traffic flow is controlled by road markings, traffic islands, signals, and signs. These help guide drivers safely. You must always obey traffic signs, signals, and road markings.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has a sharp right turn followed by a sharp left turn.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Never stop, back up, or cross the median on the highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can result from:

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Too much sleep the night before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for too long without looking around. You stop paying attention and may miss traffic slowing or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate:

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: Driving at night requires increased caution because:

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as clearly as they can during the day. You must use your headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise, or whenever people or vehicles are not visible for 500 feet.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights are working properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see well. Take all these steps to keep yourself and other drivers safe on the road.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that pedestrians cross here. Watch for people in the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: Texting while driving is:

options.text: Legal, but only for non-probationary license holders.

questions.explanation: In Indiana, drivers cannot type or read text messages or emails while driving. The only exception is using your device to call emergency services.

questions.question: This is a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a yield sign. Slow down to check for traffic and let pedestrians and other vehicles cross before you. Only stop if necessary.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, you should stay away from them. Don't look at them or make gestures that could upset them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly when you drive.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road work.
Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead has a sharp turn (in this case, to the right). Slow down before reaching this sharp curve, just as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger instead of the road while driving.
Only watches the car directly ahead.

questions.explanation: Don't get distracted by passengers, searching for things, reading, looking at scenery, or daydreaming. Keep watching the road, check your mirrors often, and look at your gauges regularly. These habits keep you focused and safe.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Let your car slow down before using the brakes.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for cars behind you to stop in time. When stopping, release the gas first to slow down. Then press the brake gently and steadily to stop smoothly.

questions.question: This sign is used to prevent:

options.text: Entrance from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entrance from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic moves one way only. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: To make sure your health doesn't cause unsafe driving, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only when you are physically able.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limits and only drive when it is safe for you to do so.

questions.question: A green arrow with a red light means that:

options.text: You may only go straight ahead.
You may only go in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only go in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points. Only proceed if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn of railroad crossings ahead. Watch for trains when you see this sign.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles work the same way.
Not tell your friend you don't know the vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid upsetting your friend.
Take time to learn where everything is and how the vehicle works before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time to learn where everything is and how the vehicle works before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning where the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn are located and how to use them. Have any problems fixed before driving.
